extra_quotes: In this Letter, we propose that the uniform metallic FM order is stabilized by the prominent quantum metric near topological band crossing points at K and K ′, which reconstructs the magnetic instability in the dice metal and tips the density-wave instability toward a uniform FM order.
Importantly, our analysis based on random phase approximation (RPA) and Hartree–Fock theory predicts a remarkably high Curie temperature above room temperature for the 2D FM order.

For the realistic multi-orbital model of YCl with the onsite Hubbard parameter U d2z = 0.9 eV derived from first-principles estimates [30], we find that χ RPAs (q, T) remains sharply peaked at q = 0 for all temperatures down to the critical temperature (in-set of Fig. 3(c)), and the Stoner condition yields a critical temperature of T RPA c ≃ 1042 K.

To complement the RPA analysis with a more microscopic treatment of local magnetic moments on inequivalent sublattice sites, we perform self-consistent Hartree–Fock (HF) calculations based on the same ab inito-based Hubbard model of YCl and the same model parameters.

Notably, while our RPA and HF framework neglects spatial and thermal spin fluctuations which may affect the exact value of Curie temperatures [44], the consistent high temperature scales obtained from the two independent approaches, T RPA c ≃ 1042 K and T HF c ≃ 1075 K, indicate a robust uniform ferromagnetic order with transition temperatures a few times of the room temperature of 300 K.
